land.text: the Brittonic lands of the Old North (Yr Hen Ogledd) around the Solway and Cumbria, inside Cliopatria's Brythons shape of 540-554

predecessors.note: The Rheged page's infobox says 'Preceded by the Hen Ogledd' and 'Yr Hen Ogledd (The Old North) c.500'. The start year c. 550 is the first year of Urien's dated reign, 'Urien Rheged, (c. 550 – 590)'; the page gives no founding year, and Cliopatria's own Rheged shape begins in 592, when Brythons falls from 64,870 to 51,613 km2 (Rheged 11,637 plus Dunoting about 1,500). Until then Cliopatria's Brythons shapes contain this land, so the Brythons dossier should remove Rheged's land from c. 550.

land.text: Northumbria's 647 shape, which grows by 12,000 km2 over 644-646 and takes Cumbria

successors.note: 'Rheged was annexed by Northumbria, some time before AD 730'; the page suggests a 'peaceful takeover' after Oswiu's marriage to Rieinmelth, 'probably in 638'. The end year 646 is Cliopatria's.

land.text: the part of Rheged north of Penrith (lat 54.66), which Strathclyde held at its greatest extent, 'to the River Eamont at Penrith' (Strathclyde page); a polygon because no name fits

successors.note: Not a 646 handover. Infobox 'Succeeded by Northumbria and Strathclyde'; 'Around the year 900 ... large areas west of the Pennines came under Strathclyde' (Rheged page). The Strathclyde page (repair pass) has the kingdom 'expanded south to the Cumbrian Mountains, into the former lands of Rheged' (undated) and, 'at its greatest extent in the 10th century', from Loch Lomond 'to the River Eamont at Penrith'. Cliopatria's Strathclyde shapes (644-1033) all end at lat 54.953 and never overlap Rheged, so Strathclyde's own 647 shape was the wrong land spec; this one is Rheged's land north of Penrith, taken c. 900 or later. The 646 land goes to Northumbria.

capitals.name: Carlisle (Luguvalium)
capitals.note: Infobox capital. 'Later legend associates Urien with the city of Carlisle'; the page has no year for the seat. Dated from the c. 550 start; the seat itself is undated.

correction.text: the 592 shape drawn back to c. 550 (Urien's dated reign); the page gives no extent before 592, so the extent of Rheged before 592 is unknown

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 550-591 (Cliopatria starts in 592): the Rheged page lists 'Urien Rheged, (c. 550 – 590), about whom survive eight songs of Taliesin' among the kings who 'may have ruled in Rheged', and the Urien page puts his war on Lindisfarne in the Theodric and Hussa years (572-593). The page gives no extent for these years, so the 592 shape (Cumbria, 11,637 km2) is used; the extent before 592 is unknown. Cliopatria's Brythons shapes of 540-591 hold this land and should lose it.

Cliopatria's first Rheged shape; the new 550 keyframe carries it back to c. 550. 592-616, 11,637 km2 (lat 53.33-54.95, lon -3.70 to -2.13). The infobox gives no area. The page's extent is 'a large part of modern Cumbria as well as areas of Dumfries and Galloway', with Lancashire possible ('Rochdale ... with even less certainty') and Dumfries and Galloway only 'at least in one period of its history'. The shape runs south of Rochdale to lat 53.33 and stops at the Solway (lat 54.95), so it takes no Dumfries and Galloway; both edges are uncertain on the page and the shape is left as drawn.

617-637, 11,723 km2, 86 km2 more than 592. Edwin of Deira ruled Northumbria about 616-633 and 'the Isle of Man and the lands of Gwynedd in Northern Wales were incorporated into Northumbria' (Northumbria page); the page does not name Rheged. Rhun of Rheged 'is said to have baptised Edwin' but 'may merely have stood sponsor' (Rheged page). Shape left as drawn.

638-643, 11,953 km2, 230 km2 more than 617 (north edge to lat 55.02). 638 is the year the Rheged page gives, 'probably', for Oswiu's marriage to Rieinmelth ('it is possible that it was a peaceful takeover') and the year the Hen Ogledd page gives for the siege of Din Eidyn. The page does not explain the growth.

644-646, 11,953 km2, the same as 638. Cliopatria's Strathclyde begins in 644 along Rheged's northern edge (lat 54.95). The end of Rheged is undated on the pages opened: 'annexed by Northumbria, some time before AD 730'. 646 is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Cumbria with the Solway shores, Carlisle as seat, drawn as the 592 shape because the page gives no earlier extent

ledger.note: c. 550: Rheged under Urien, the first king of the dynasty with dates on the page ('Urien Rheged, (c. 550 – 590)'). The page gives no founding year ('Yr Hen Ogledd (The Old North) c.500' is the Hen Ogledd era in the infobox, and Coel Hen is 'if he has some historicity'), so 550 bridges a silence. Cliopatria's Rheged shape begins in 592; its Brythons shape holds the land before. Reviewer eu-11-f: the first draft started at 592, after the 572-593 war on Lindisfarne.

region.text: the northern strip of the 638 shape (lat 54.95-55.02)

ledger.note: 638: Cliopatria's Rheged grows by 230 km2 on its northern edge. No opened page reports it; 638 is also the 'probable' year of Oswiu's marriage to Rieinmelth of Rheged (Rheged page). Repair pass: the Rhun ap Urien and Rhun of Rheged pages returned url_not_found and nothing else opened reports the growth; still confidence 1.

region.text: the whole kingdom, Cumbria and the Solway

ledger.note: 646: Rheged is gone from the map, absorbed by Northumbria. The page dates it only as 'annexed by Northumbria, some time before AD 730' and suggests a peaceful takeover after Oswiu's marriage to Rieinmelth, 'probably in 638'; Royth is named as 'possibly the last king of Rheged'. The year is Cliopatria's (Northumbria grows to 47,772 km2 in 647). Repair pass: the Elmet page names Rheged but gives no year for its annexation and does not mention 646; the Strathclyde page has Strathclyde expanding 'into the former lands of Rheged' (undated); still Cliopatria's year, confidence 1.

wars.name: Urien of Rheged's siege of Lindisfarne

zones.text: Lindisfarne (Old Welsh Medcaut) and the Bernician coast

wars.outcome: Urien 'penned the Anglo-Saxons in at Lindisfarne' with an alliance of Rhydderch Hen, Gwallog and Morgan; he 'was killed at the instigation of Morgan'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Years are the Historia Brittonum synchronisms as the Urien page reports them (Theodric 572-579, Hussa 585-92); the page puts Urien's death anywhere from 572 to after 597. The Rheged page says his victories over the Anglian chieftains of Bernicia were 'in the second half of the 6th century'. Inside the dossier's life now that the start is c. 550 (it began at 592 in the first draft).

certainty.note: The extent of Rheged is disputed on every side (Lancashire, Dumfries and Galloway, Catterick); no frontier is sharp.

notes:
Kingdom of Rheged (4 Cliopatria shapes, 592-646; dossier life c. 550-646), five pages (budget up to 5) plus a repair pass that opened Elmet and Strathclyde (Rhun ap Urien and Rhun of Rheged: url_not_found).
START IS c. 550, A BRIDGE (confidence 1); THE END IS CLIOPATRIA'S (confidence 1): the Rheged page has no founding year but dates Urien 'c. 550 – 590', so the dossier starts there and a new keyframe carries Cliopatria's 592 shape back to 550 (the first draft started at 592, after the 572-593 war it carried). Cliopatria's Brythons shapes of 540-591 hold this land and the Brythons dossier should remove it. The page says only that Rheged was 'annexed by Northumbria, some time before AD 730'. The Oswiu page does not mention Rheged's annexation and the Northumbria page names Rheged nowhere. A gap-filler should open 'Oswiu', 'Kingdom of Northumbria' history sections, 'Elmet' (for Edwin's conquests) and the Catraeth / Argoed Llwyfain battle pages.
SHAPE vs PAGE: the Cliopatria shape has no Dumfries and Galloway and runs south of Rochdale; see the 592 verdict. The Strathclyde dossier (Cliopatria row from 644) should say whether Galloway was Rheged's.
SUCCESSORS: Northumbria (from 647 in Cliopatria) and Strathclyde per the infobox; Strathclyde took the area only c. 900 on the Rheged page and in an undated southern expansion on its own page, so its land spec is now Rheged's land north of Penrith (a polygon), not a 646 handover.
THIN, STILL: the 638 growth and the 646 annexation have no page (Elmet and Strathclyde are silent on the year; the Rhun pages failed).
Ruler list not given: the infobox names Meirchion Gul, Cynfarch Oer, Urien and Owain mab Urien and the page gives no regnal dates apart from Urien 'c. 550 - 590'.
